title: Volume and surface area of prism and cylinder
summary: Use cross-sections and nets to calculate prism and cylinder measures.
objectives: Calculate a prism volume from cross-sectional area and length.
Build total surface area from end faces and lateral faces.

blocks.text: Use cross-sections and nets to calculate prism and cylinder measures. Keep every measurement in compatible units before substituting.

A prism has a constant cross-section, so volume=cross-sectional area×length. A cylinder is a circular prism with volume πr²h. Surface area unfolds every exposed face: two congruent ends plus the lateral surface.

For a right prism, the lateral area is perimeter of cross-section×length. For a cylinder, curved area=2πrh and total surface area=2πr²+2πrh. Check whether a container is open or closed before including circular ends.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: A closed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. Find its total surface area in terms of π.

content.text: The two circular ends have area 2πr²=18π.

sections.verification_note: A closed cylinder includes two ends; every term has square units.

blocks.text: Do not confuse diameter with radius. Volume uses cubic units; surface area uses square units. For prisms, the cross-sectional area is multiplied by the prism length, which may not be the vertical dimension in the sketch.

prompt.text: A prism has cross-sectional area 15 cm² and length 8 cm. Find its volume in cm³.
